title: Spark Plug Replacement
summary: Ignition blueprint for quoting spark plugs without overstating engine fitment when cylinder count or access is not yet confirmed.
symptoms: Rough idle, misfire, hesitation, or hard start
Worn plug gap or fouling found during diagnosis
Flashing check engine light during active misfire
inspect_first: Mileage, maintenance history, and correct plug type
Misfire codes and whether the miss follows a cylinder
Coil boots, plug wells, oil intrusion, and carbon tracking
Access restrictions from intake manifolds or rear banks
likely_causes: Incorrect plug gap or wrong plug type
Ignition coil, injector, vacuum leak, or compression issue misdiagnosed as plugs
repair_overview: Confirm plugs are due or contributing to the fault.
Remove coils or wires carefully and inspect boots and wells.
Install correct plugs to specification and avoid cross-threading.
Verify idle quality, misfire counters, and road behavior after repair.
common_mistakes: Calling plugs bad before checking coils, injectors, or compression on a repeated misfire
Using the wrong heat range or plug design
Ignoring oil in plug wells that can damage new boots
estimate_guidance: Use generic spark plug labeling when engine configuration is unknown.
Add access labor when intake removal or rear-bank access is required.
Recommend coil boot or ignition coil inspection when misfire history is present.

recommended_repairs.description: Use when the misfire is cylinder-specific or load-related.

recommended_repairs.title: Misfire Diagnostic Path
recommended_repairs.description: Use when plugs are only one possible cause.

diagnostic_context.intro: Spark plug replacement connects tightly to misfire diagnosis, but plugs should not hide coil, injector, vacuum leak, or compression evidence.
